newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 17.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-April 17.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Thursday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's United Front coalition will choose a new leader to replace caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda at a meeting on Friday, spokesman says

Jaipal Reddy said the alliance's decision-making Steering Committee will meet at 3 p.m. (0930 GMT) but is expected to adjourn due to the death in hospital on Thursday of veteran politician Biju Patnaik, a leader of Deve Gowda's Janata Dal party
** Influential leftist bloc in ousted United Front coalition cautions allies against naming a new candidate for the top job unless the Congress withdraws its formal claim to form a government
The four-party communist-led Left Front says that Congress president Sitaram Kesri was still his party's official candidate for the prime minister's job
** The toppled United Front coalition says there is a "distinct possibility" a new government under its leadership will be forged in the next few days

** While India puzzles who will succeed defeated Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, investors in the country are more concerned whether Finance Minister P. Chidambaram will keep his job, equity analysts say
** The Asian Development Bank says it expects Indian industry to grow at a robust 11.5 percent in the financial years 1997/98 (April-March) and 1998/99
"Industry will continue as an engine of economic growth and should increase by 11.5 percent in 1997 and 1998," ADB says in its annual report on India
** India's central bank has taken the first major steps to integrate the country's money and foreign exchange markets with the global market, bankers and analysts say
They say the central bank's credit policy for the first six months of 1997/98 (April-March) marks a step towards integrating Indian markets with international markets
** The prospect of capacity shortages and high demand growth in the oil sector fuelling high earnings growth will attract international investors into oil stocks, analysts say
** India must speed up the pace of divestment in its state-run oil companies or face the prospect of losing badly-needed aid funding, an official of the Asian Development Bank says

** India's average annual economic growth is projected at seven percent in the five years to 2000, according to the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific, the Observer newspaper says.
MARKETS:
** Major Indian stock markets, except Madras were closed on Wednesday for a Hindu festival. They will reopen Thursday, and close for a Moslem festival on Friday
The Bombay Stock Exchange top 30 index closed on Tuesday up 52.72, or 1.61 percent, at 3,647.44
Delhi index closed up 7.58 points at 760.63, Calcutta index was up 1.06 at 100.81
Madras index closed 11.08 points up at 3,481.90
-- Bombay Newsroom, + 91-22-265 9000
